summary: This program counts from 1 to 10 with a while loop, but skips printing any number that divides evenly by 3, so you see 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10.

lines.text: The modulo operator gives the remainder of a division, so a remainder of zero means `i` is an exact multiple of 3 and should be skipped.

This increment has to happen before `continue`, because `continue` jumps straight back to the condition and any line below it would never run. Forget this one and `i` stays at 3 forever, giving an infinite loop.
`continue` abandons the rest of this pass through the loop and starts the next one, which is how the multiples of 3 get skipped instead of printed.
The normal path needs its own increment as well, since the loop only advances when you move the counter yourself.
